title: Option in the UI to use WPS instead of a password when connecting to a new Wi-Fi network
line: Wi-Fi networks whose router supports WPS can now be joined by pressing the router's WPS button instead of typing the password.
explanation: NetworkManager already supports push-button WPS: when it activates a WPA-PSK connection without a password on a router that advertises WPS push button, it starts WPS enrollment and asks the secret agent for the password with a flag saying WPS is active. Plasma ignored both sides: the applet always required a password before connecting a new network, and the password dialog never mentioned WPS. The applet now reads the access point's WPS flag and, when it is set, shows a "Connect Using Router's WPS Button" button under the password field that starts the connection without a password; the password dialog says "Press the WPS button on your router, or enter the password…" when NetworkManager reports WPS as active, and closes on its own once the router button is pressed.

commits.message:
applet, kded: offer connecting with the router's WPS button

NetworkManager can join a Wi-Fi network through push-button WPS, but
Plasma never let people start it nor told them about it. The applet now
offers it below the password field and the password dialog mentions it.

BUG: 459277

media.caption: A new network whose router supports WPS: the applet only offers a password field.
The same network now offers "Connect Using Router's WPS Button" under the password field.
Password dialog while NetworkManager has WPS push button active: no mention of WPS.
The dialog now tells the user to press the WPS button on the router or type the password.
Other cases: wrong password with WPS active gets the hint; without WPS the texts are unchanged.
